I am about as much of an "Anti-Apple" fanboy (if that is what you want to call it) as you will find.

Yet, the conspiratard in me simply cannot help but draw the line connecting the direct refusal of Apple to give the feds their encryption key and the drop in their stock.

Why would smartphones decline. Are we going to go back to phone/text only phonies? I don't think so. The watches aren't all that. They still require a smart phone for the most part. We aren't going to be putting tablets up to our face (Which, let's face it, if we all went tablets only, Apple would still be just fine).

So in this alleged "Decline" in smart phone sales, what are we going to replace them with? And in an Article like this, a decline in "Global Smart Phone Sales" should also note the potential impact this could have on others. Samsung, LG... Nokia (LOL, J/K) but you get my point.

TL;DR Apple declines feds.. Stock drops. Market says We aren't going to want cell phones but fails to say what will replace them.

edit: The more I think about this, the less I understand why Smart Phone sales would plummit. The article gives no notion of what will come behind to relieve Smart Phones. I really, the more I think about it, feel like this reads as a warning to would be investors considering investing in a business that won't comply with federal overstepping.

There used to be a kind of "need" to upgrade every 6-12 months.

Now phones are fast enough and tougher so they last longer. People don't feel as much desire to upgrade as much. So if they used to get a new one every year and now it's 2 years. That mean sales are cut in half.

Apple stock has been way over inflated for years. The bubble is bursting.

Also people aren't getting a phone, tablet, laptop, and desktop as much anymore. A phone and laptop or tablet do the majority of computing now.

Also with emerging things like being able to plug your phone into a tablet sized screen or desktop monitor will further lower sales of multiple devices.

Certainly people are not buying desktops nearly as much. But as indicated through this article. Apple doesn't rely on their desktop/pc sales much. They have also already felt a great deal of the Desktop drop burden. The Desktop sales will not tank them in the manner that is being discussed in this article/happening to them now"

I will give you the "Stronger phones" "lasting longer" notion. I must admit, somehow, that did not occur to me and that does probably make up a great deal of what is being discussed here. As it stands right now, Apple sales continue to skyrocket without any end in sight. I appreciate that their stock is inflated. Yes, I suppose that also genuinely warrants some decline in value as a principle. I would also add in regards to the stock products aside. A companies cash on hand can also hold some influence on the price of the share. COH warrants the idea of potential, even if it is never really spent, people invest in the off chance that the company does something extraordinary.

I do believe that apple still owns their market. Apple fanboys and girls (Of which there are annoyingly many, I assure you) will continue to drop their current Iphone for the allure of a shiny new device. With Iphone 7 I am beyond confident that Apple will get their sales. I would even venture that they will have record sales that exceed the record sales that Apple hit in Sept of this year.

Assuming the Iphone 7 a success. We can at least lead to the notion that Apple will not experience this cell phone squeeze too much until potentially the Iphone 8. Assuming that, we can see at least another good 2 - 3-4 years of worthy trading/investing into Apple as a stock. If anything, this Apple stock fallout seems prematurely timed or the result of industry panic.

Maybe I'm very very wrong. Honestly, I hope I am and we will see sooner-ish than later-ish.

edit: Upon further delving into this. It appears that people dislike the Iphone 6s but loved the Iphone 6. Although it does appear as if the Iphone 6s suddenly suffered a stark decline in interest/sales broke 10 million preorders. A record set by the 6 a year earlier.

In a nutshell technical maturity. Just look at the PC market. We don't upgrade nearly as frequently as we used to as the power of a 5 year old PC is still just fine for most tasks. Smartphones are going the same way.
